claims_supported: A coding agent can iterate on one mutable training file under a fixed wall-clock budget and append every result.
relevance: Operational precedent for a bounded autonomous experiment loop; this project adds preregistration, multi-objective metrics and stronger integrity controls.
title: karpathy/autoresearch

claims_supported: Retrieval can attach a very large explicit memory to a smaller language model without proportional dense parameter growth.
relevance: Direct evidence that knowledge capacity and parametric compute can be partially separated, while leaving retrieval and controller costs in the system boundary.
title: Improving language models by retrieving from trillions of tokens

claims_supported: A recurrent model can learn a variable number of computation steps and allocate more work to harder inputs.
relevance: Prior art for compute scaling with problem difficulty rather than using a fixed depth for every input.
title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks

claims_supported: Sparse gating can increase parameter capacity far faster than active per-example computation.
relevance: Strong prior art against claiming that conditional knowledge activation is itself novel; routing and end-to-end memory traffic remain open issues.
title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer

claims_supported: A neural controller can learn to interact with an external differentiable memory on algorithmic tasks.
relevance: Prior art for decoupling controller computation from memory, and a warning about scalability and training stability.
title: Neural Turing Machines

claims_supported: A differentiable neural computer can learn read/write use of an external memory on graph and structured reasoning tasks.
relevance: A close predecessor for learned memory access and persistent structured state; any ACC/SCCS claim must distinguish itself empirically.
title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory

claims_supported: Learned local update rules can produce persistent and regenerative global structures.
relevance: Concrete prior art for local, event-like computation and emergent self-organization, but not evidence of general reasoning.
title: Growing Neural Cellular Automata

claims_supported: HDC/VSA combines distributed vectors with algebraic operations for structured representations.
relevance: Landscape source for a non-token, compositional representation family; empirical claims must be checked against the cited primary studies.
title: A Survey on Hyperdimensional Computing aka Vector Symbolic Architectures, Part I

claims_supported: Wake-sleep program induction can learn reusable symbolic abstractions and improve later search.
relevance: Direct prior art for discovering primitives and compiling repeated solution fragments into a growing library.
title: DreamCoder: Bootstrapping Inductive Program Synthesis with Wake-Sleep Library Learning

claims_supported: Standard sequence models can fail controlled systematic-compositional generalization splits.
relevance: Motivates explicit compositional OOD tests, while later systems require updated baselines rather than treating SCAN as permanently unsolved.
title: Generalization without Systematicity

claims_supported: Codex desktop scheduled tasks can run against a local project and return to an existing chat; the computer and app must remain running.
relevance: Defines the native persistence mechanism used instead of an external agent API.
title: Scheduled tasks

claims_supported: Codex reads repository AGENTS.md guidance before work and layers project-local instructions by directory.
relevance: Defines how the scientific doctrine and operational constraints persist across Codex runs.
title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md

claims_supported: Corpus-guided top-down synthesis can extract reusable DSL abstractions from solved programs.
Stitch reports 3-4 orders of magnitude lower runtime and 2 orders lower memory than the compared DreamCoder library learner at comparable or better compressivity.
relevance: Shows that a compact library extractor is feasible, while compressivity of a known corpus must not be confused with held-out transfer.
title: Top-Down Synthesis for Library Learning

claims_supported: Switch Transformer keeps active computation approximately fixed while increasing sparse parameter capacity.
The paper identifies complexity, communication cost and training instability as barriers for sparse MoE.
relevance: Strong baseline and warning that sparse active FLOPs are not an end-to-end efficiency proof.
title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity

claims_supported: Expert Choice gives each expert fixed capacity while allowing a variable number of experts per token.
At matched computational resources it reports more than 2x faster convergence than compared top-k routing and stronger downstream results.
relevance: Motivates heterogeneous learned routing controls, but does not remove router, memory or serving costs.
title: Mixture-of-Experts with Expert Choice Routing

claims_supported: A learned router can dynamically compose reusable nonlinear function blocks per input in multi-task learning.
The reported CIFAR-100 setup matched cross-stitch performance with 85 percent less training time.
relevance: Direct prior art for functional experts and recursive routing; a NEXTAI test must add held-out compositions and full routing cost.
title: Routing Networks: Adaptive Selection of Non-linear Functions for Multi-Task Learning

claims_supported: The degree and placement of modularity strongly affect systematic generalization in neural module networks.
Intermediate modularity at the image-encoder stage improved novel-combination generalization across controlled VQA studies.
relevance: Warns against treating maximal modularity as intrinsically better and motivates explicit OOD composition ablations.
title: How Modular Should Neural Module Networks Be for Systematic Generalization?

claims_supported: Causal predictors can be identified by invariance across suitable environments and interventions.
Purely observational predictive associations can fail when predictor variables are intervened upon.
relevance: Direct prior art for the invariance test used by the factorized learner; this project is not novel causal discovery theory.
title: Causal Inference by using Invariant Prediction: Identification and Confidence Intervals

claims_supported: Bayesian causal discovery can jointly infer causal structure and uncertain intervention targets from multiple interventional conditions.
The reported method evaluates synthetic causal discovery and simulated gene-expression tasks with limited intervention information.
relevance: A substantially stronger prior-art baseline for the adversarial missing-intervention setting than the repository's exact invariant search.
title: BaCaDI: Bayesian Causal Discovery with Unknown Interventions

claims_supported: Causal learning methods can be evaluated by predicting effects of interventions on unseen test data rather than only recovering a true DAG.
relevance: Direct precedent for using held-out intervention prediction as the capability metric in EXP-0011 and EXP-0012.
title: Causal learning without DAGs

claims_supported: Directional chain-reaction systems can be identifiable from blocking interventions under explicit structural assumptions.
The paper provides finite-sample guarantees and synthetic chain-reaction evaluations where observational heuristics fail.
relevance: Very close prior art to the chain experiment, showing that EXP-0011's structural recovery is an expected special case rather than a novel principle.
title: Causal Discovery in Action: Learning Chain-Reaction Mechanisms from Interventions

claims_supported: A task-agnostic recurrent core can execute compositional programs stored in persistent key-value program memory.
The reported generalization uses fully supervised execution traces and domain-specific encoders.
relevance: Direct prior art and a critical supervision-cost control for HYP-0009; a local pointer-machine result would not by itself be novel.
title: Neural Programmer-Interpreters

claims_supported: CLRS provides a unified benchmark spanning sorting, searching, dynamic programming, graph, string and geometric algorithms.
Evaluation on one synthetic algorithm family does not establish broad neural algorithmic reasoning.
relevance: Sets the transfer standard for HYP-0009 and prevents promotion from a single pointer or tape micro-world.
title: The CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark

claims_supported: Neural GPU length generalization can coexist with failures on rare highly symmetric inputs.
Curriculum and model size materially affect algorithm-learning success and must be charged or controlled.
relevance: Motivates an adversarial-pattern split in the cheapest HYP-0009 test rather than accepting average length extrapolation alone.
title: Extensions and Limitations of the Neural GPU

claims_supported: A recurrent system with symmetric interactions can implement content-addressable memory as convergence in a state-space flow.
A sufficiently informative fragment of a stored pattern can recover the full pattern in the demonstrated model.
relevance: Foundational baseline for HYP-0007; content-addressed completion by attractor dynamics is established prior art, not a new successor principle.
title: Neural networks and physical systems with emergent collective computational abilities

claims_supported: Higher-order dense associative memories can store and retrieve more patterns than classical pairwise memories.
The proposed family connects energy-based associative memory to one-hidden-layer neural networks and was demonstrated on XOR and MNIST.
relevance: A strong energy-memory control: any apparent high-capacity or nonlinear cleanup benefit must be compared with dense associative memory and fully charged retrieval scans.
title: Dense Associative Memory for Pattern Recognition

claims_supported: Modern continuous Hopfield networks admit single-pattern, metastable subset-average and global-average fixed points.
Their update is equivalent to transformer attention and evaluates stored patterns during retrieval.
relevance: Prevents interpreting one-step soft retrieval or attention-equivalent full-memory scoring as a computation breakthrough; metastable averages are a registered failure mode.
title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need

claims_supported: A learned energy over outputs can support iterative reasoning through repeated minimization steps.
The reported method varied inference effort with task difficulty and evaluated graph, continuous and nested algorithmic problems.
relevance: Direct prior art for learned energy-based reasoning; a local toy relaxation result must isolate a new scaling or composition signature rather than claim the general mechanism.
title: Learning Iterative Reasoning through Energy Minimization

claims_supported: Annealed energy landscapes with score and energy supervision were used for iterative reasoning and OOD difficulty generalization.
The reported evaluations include Sudoku, matrix completion and larger-graph path finding.
relevance: Shows that stable learned energy reasoning may require annealing and rich supervision; the minimal quick must not hide those costs or overclaim from hand-set local potentials.
title: Learning Iterative Reasoning through Energy Diffusion

claims_supported: Rete compiles production patterns into a stateful matching network instead of rescanning every pattern and object on each cycle.
Its applicability assumes compilable patterns, constant objects and relatively slow changes to working memory.
relevance: Strong algorithmic baseline for HYP-0003: sparse event activation and persistent partial matches are established production-system techniques whose indexing and update costs must be counted.
title: Rete: A fast algorithm for the many pattern/many object pattern match problem

claims_supported: The Chemical Abstract Machine formalizes computation as reactions over structured multisets with locality and membranes.
The chemical metaphor for concurrent local rewriting predates ACC/SCCS and is an operational semantics rather than a learned architecture.
relevance: Foundational chemical-computation prior art; a semantic-reaction candidate needs learned reusable rules and a measured scaling distinction rather than the metaphor alone.
title: The Chemical Abstract Machine

claims_supported: A shared learned rule over local cell neighborhoods can produce persistent and regenerative global patterns.
The demonstrated model uses repeated local neural updates, stochastic cell masks and backpropagation through iterative dynamics.
relevance: Closest evidence for learned local self-organization, but it does not establish sparse semantic rule discovery or K-independent event routing.
title: Growing Neural Cellular Automata

claims_supported: Neural Production Systems learn rule templates, score their match to entities and apply selected rules to update entity properties.
The reported factorization supports future-state prediction and extrapolation from fewer to more objects in visual environments.
relevance: Direct learned-rule predecessor for HYP-0003; rule binding, sparse interaction and systematic extrapolation cannot be claimed as novel without a distinct event-cost or continual-update result.
title: Neural Production Systems

claims_supported: Graph neural networks can learn finite discrete graph-cellular-automaton transition rules on arbitrary graphs.
Reported tasks include imitation of local dynamics and convergence to a target state.
relevance: Provides the matched full-sweep learned local-rule baseline and prevents treating graph-local transition learning itself as an ACC/SCCS novelty.
title: Learning Graph Cellular Automata

claims_supported: Jointly learning heterogeneous modules and their composition creates non-stationarity, collapse and overfitting challenges absent from fixed routing.
Routing without informative meta-features can perform near random or collapse, while routing depth worsens optimization instability.
relevance: Direct warning for HYP-0010: a supplied route or easy task label would hide the central learning problem, so route features and held-out compositions must be explicit.
title: Routing Networks and the Challenges of Modular and Compositional Computation

claims_supported: Modular teacher-student systems can identify reusable components from demonstrations and generalize to unseen compositions under stated identifiability conditions.
Modular architectures can otherwise collapse to monolithic solutions that memorize observed task combinations.
relevance: Closest positive prior art for the proposed heterogeneous-composition test; NEXTAI must measure routing and end-to-end cost rather than claim compositional module discovery as novel.
title: Discovering modular solutions that generalize compositionally

claims_supported: Sparse layers route each token to a small subset of expert parameters but balanced expert use is difficult to learn.
BASE formulates token-to-expert routing as balanced linear assignment rather than relying on auxiliary balancing losses.
relevance: Strong sparse-expert systems baseline: expert activation alone is not the full cost, and routing balance or assignment machinery must be counted.
title: BASE Layers: Simplifying Training of Large, Sparse Models

claims_supported: On compositional reasoning tasks, the empirically optimal number of active experts increases with task difficulty.
The reported theory balances approximation and estimation error and predicts intermediate rather than minimal sparsity.
relevance: Current direct prior art against a fixed-top-1 thesis; the benchmark must scale active modules with registered composition depth and test whether dormant-expert K remains decoupled.
title: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Compositional Generalization: Empirical Evidence and Theoretical Foundations of Optimal Sparsity

claims_supported: Program synthesis can infer explicit programs from input-output examples, whereas program induction can predict outputs through a latent program representation.
On RobustFill's task, neural synthesis outperformed a comparable induction model and could be trained for expected input noise, while outcomes depended on the evaluation metric and application.
relevance: Direct matched prior art for whole-I/O learning; NEXTAI must compare explicit search with latent execution and cannot treat either route as novel.
title: RobustFill: Neural Program Learning under Noisy I/O

claims_supported: Neural Programmer-Interpreters combine a shared recurrent core, key-value program memory and environment interfaces to compose and execute reusable programs.
The reported NPI was trained with fully supervised execution traces and curriculum rather than only weak whole-program input-output labels.
relevance: Foundational learned-VM prior art and a decisive caveat for EXP-0013: supplied traces can carry compositional structure, so the next benchmark must remove them.
title: Neural Programmer-Interpreters

claims_supported: DreamCoder jointly learns a library of program components and a neural search policy across tasks specified by one or a few examples.
Wake-sleep learning and E-graph refactoring progressively build reusable abstractions and improve the number and speed of solved synthesis tasks.
relevance: Strong explicit-search and learned-library predecessor; any learned VM must beat a counted enumerative/MDL control rather than omit search or library-construction costs.
title: DreamCoder: Bootstrapping Inductive Program Synthesis with Wake-Sleep Library Learning

claims_supported: A differentiable Forth interpreter can train program-sketch slots end to end from input-output objectives.
Its demonstrated gains explicitly leverage supplied procedural structure at varying levels rather than inducing an unconstrained machine from scratch.
relevance: Bounds novelty and exposes the program-sketch confound: interpreter priors and any fixed action vocabulary must be disclosed and ablated in the whole-I/O test.
title: Programming with a Differentiable Forth Interpreter

claims_supported: Self-adjusting computation records data and control dependencies in dynamic dependence graphs and re-executes affected computation while reusing unaffected work.
Incremental speedups depend on trace stability; for some modifications change propagation is no faster than recomputation, and trace storage grows with represented dependencies.
relevance: Strongest matched classical baseline for HYP-0011: dependency tracking and local invalidation are established, so a learned compiler needs a distinct transfer or cost signature beyond DDG change propagation.
title: An Experimental Analysis of Self-Adjusting Computation

claims_supported: First-class names identify computations for reuse across differing program runs and can outperform purely structural matching.
Nominal Adapton proves from-scratch consistency and detects ambiguous name reuse, but the programmer controls the naming strategy.
relevance: Direct warning against hiding task identity in supplied stable names; the benchmark must use byte-different structures and charge learned or classical canonicalization before reuse.
title: Incremental Computation with Names

claims_supported: Practical graph isomorphism and canonical labeling are addressed by refinement-individualization methods implemented in nauty and Traces.
Canonicalization is a classical algorithmic problem with specialized methods and difficult graph classes.
relevance: Makes exact canonical labeling the decisive control for cross-structure cache transfer; learned signatures cannot claim novelty merely by matching isomorphic DAGs.
title: Practical Graph Isomorphism, II

claims_supported: Message-passing GNN representations follow neighborhood aggregation and have graph-discrimination limits tied to the Weisfeiler-Lehman test.
Graph Isomorphism Networks reach the stated WL expressiveness bound within that model class but still cannot distinguish every graph pair.
relevance: Sets the strongest relevant learned-signature expectation and an explicit failure mode: a minimal learned canonicalizer may collide on structurally confusable graphs even when exact canonicalization succeeds.
title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?

claims_supported: E-graphs compactly represent equivalence classes of expressions under congruence and support non-destructive equality saturation.
Rebuilding amortizes congruence maintenance, while e-class analyses integrate domain-specific facts needed for valid transformations.
relevance: Strong semantic-equivalence baseline: reuse across rewrites requires equivalence machinery and invariant maintenance whose work and state must be counted.
title: egg: Fast and Extensible Equality Saturation

claims_supported: Graph neural networks can learn independent graph embeddings for similarity reasoning.
Graph Matching Networks jointly reason over a graph pair with cross-graph attention and outperform reported domain-specific baselines on control-flow-graph function similarity.
relevance: Closest learned graph-pair alignment control for opaque rewrite representations; similarity scores are not certificates of semantic equivalence, so exact near-equivalent rejection and matching cost must be measured.
title: Graph Matching Networks for Learning the Similarity of Graph Structured Objects

claims_supported: Neural Theorem Provers replace symbolic unification with an RBF similarity over learned dense symbol representations.
They learn symbol similarities and function-free first-order rules of predefined structure for multi-hop knowledge-base inference.
relevance: Direct positive precedent for learned soft atom identity, but its approximate unification and supplied proof machinery do not establish collision-free exact reuse.
title: End-to-End Differentiable Proving

claims_supported: Differentiable ILP learns continuous representations of logic programs from positive and negative examples through backpropagation.
The reported system handles symbolic benchmark tasks, ambiguous inputs and up to 20 percent mislabelled training data in its noise study.
relevance: Positive rule-acquisition control showing that differentiable search can learn explicit structure, while the supplied logical language and full training-space cost must remain inside NEXTAI's boundary.
title: Learning Explanatory Rules from Noisy Data

claims_supported: Neural Logic Machines learn lifted rules on small tasks and report perfect size generalization on several relational and decision tasks.
Their architecture supplies tensorized predicates, logic connectives, quantifier-like expansion and reduction, and a configured maximum predicate arity.
relevance: Strong positive OOD neural-symbolic baseline and a warning that exact-looking generalization can depend on a hand-designed logical substrate carrying the invariances.
title: Neural Logic Machines

claims_supported: On synthetic ground-truth relations, the studied Neural Theorem Prover failed to recover relationships beyond the simplest settings and degraded as the number of predicates increased.
Propagating gradients through additional proof paths improved rule recovery, showing exploration policy is a causal training factor rather than a cosmetic optimizer detail.
relevance: Most discriminating negative prior art for opaque atom acquisition: the next test must scale confusable predicates, report every seed and separate rule discovery from approximate fact prediction.
title: Neural Theorem Provers Do Not Learn Rules Without Exploration

claims_supported: SEQUITUR incrementally replaces repeated phrases in a discrete sequence with recursive grammar rules.
Its two grammar constraints admit linear time and space in input length.
relevance: Makes an incremental grammar compressor the strongest classical control for discovering reusable byte motifs; repeated-pair discovery alone is established prior art.
title: Identifying Hierarchical Structure in Sequences: A Linear-Time Algorithm

claims_supported: Finite-sequence complexity can be defined through incremental reproduction of a sequence from its already observed prefix.
The induced parsing provides a classical data-dependent measure of sequential structure without a supplied motif dictionary.
relevance: Requires an incremental Lempel-Ziv parser as a no-ontology baseline and prevents attributing ordinary dictionary growth to a new learned architecture.
title: On the Complexity of Finite Sequences

claims_supported: Subword units learned with a byte-pair-encoding segmentation support open-vocabulary neural translation.
The paper explicitly compares BPE segmentation with character n-gram representations and motivates composition from smaller recurring units.
relevance: Makes greedy adjacent-pair merging and fixed n-grams mandatory controls for any learned raw-byte segmenter/composer claim.
title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

claims_supported: Compound PCFGs modulate rule probabilities with a per-sentence continuous latent variable.
Their grammar induction uses amortized variational inference for the continuous variable and dynamic programming to marginalize latent trees.
relevance: Positive neural grammar-induction precedent, but it assumes tokenized sentences and a PCFG formalism; the raw-byte test must count the missing segmentation and search work explicitly.
title: Compound Probabilistic Context-Free Grammars for Grammar Induction

claims_supported: Switching state-space models segment a time series into regimes with approximately linear dynamics and learn parameters for each regime.
The proposed variational approximation combines forward-backward HMM recursions with Kalman-filter recursions because exact posterior inference is intractable.
relevance: Establishes switching linear dynamics and their inference cost as classical controls; regime discovery alone is not a novel predictive-state principle.
title: Variational Learning for Switching State-Space Models

claims_supported: Echo-state networks use recurrent states as functions of input history and train primarily the output weights by linear regression.
The report notes initial-transient cost, a memory-capacity bound by reservoir units for iid input, and the state-size tradeoff of a large reusable reservoir.
relevance: Supplies the conventional learned recurrent control and requires charging reservoir updates, washout, regression and full state rather than treating the fixed reservoir as free.
title: The Echo State Approach to Analysing and Training Recurrent Neural Networks

claims_supported: Variance-based event triggering lets distributed sensors transmit observations sporadically to a time-varying Kalman estimator.
Trigger decisions depend on prediction variance and induce a switching Riccati iteration, so communication savings retain local filtering and trigger computation.
relevance: Closest classical event-triggered baseline and a boundary warning: every channel-side prediction and threshold check must be counted even when transmissions are sparse.
title: Event-Based State Estimation with Variance-Based Triggering

claims_supported: Predictive state can be represented by multi-step action-conditional predictions of future observations rather than a distribution over latent states.
Any system has a linear predictive-state representation using no more predictions than states in its minimal POMDP model.
relevance: Positive precedent for observable predictive state; the experiment must distinguish a learned sufficient state from ordinary AR/Kalman history and count construction plus update cost.
title: Predictive Representations of State

claims_supported: Axonal conduction delays combined with spike-timing-dependent plasticity can self-organize reproducible millisecond-precise firing patterns that are time-locked without being synchronous.
The simulated network contained many coexisting polychronous groups, but the paper presents their cognitive significance as a hypothesis rather than an end-to-end efficiency result.
relevance: Establishes learned delay-coincidence groups as prior art and requires charging synapses, delay traces, spike delivery and plasticity before claiming a distinct temporal-binding principle.
title: Polychronization: Computation with Spikes

claims_supported: Timed automata annotate finite-state transition graphs with timing constraints expressed through finitely many real-valued clocks and recognize timed words.
The paper gives finite-region constructions and also identifies expressiveness and decision-complexity limits of timed automata.
relevance: Provides the exact classical temporal-state baseline; learned spike delays must outperform rather than merely reimplement a timed finite-state recognizer.
title: A Theory of Timed Automata

claims_supported: Calendar queues bucket a discrete simulation's future event set and showed approximately constant average hold cost for the tested priority-increment distributions.
Maintaining that behavior requires bucket sizing and periodic copying as the event set grows or shrinks; poor occupancy or distributions can expose overhead.
relevance: Bounds claims that asynchronous scheduling itself is novel or free and motivates charging queue insertion, extraction, empty-bucket scans and resizing maintenance.
title: Calendar Queues: A Fast O(1) Priority Queue Implementation for the Simulation Event Set Problem

claims_supported: Liquid state machines use high-dimensional transient dynamical states to retain fading information from time-varying inputs and task-specific memoryless readouts to produce outputs.
Their computational account depends on both separation by the liquid and approximation by the readout, so reservoir evolution, state and readout training remain part of the system cost.
relevance: Supplies the conventional learned temporal control and prevents treating a fixed recurrent spiking substrate or its continuously updated state as cost-free.
title: Real-Time Computing Without Stable States: A New Framework for Neural Computation Based on Perturbations

claims_supported: Generalized binary search greedily selects the query that most evenly splits the surviving hypothesis set.

Under stated geometric conditions it identifies one of N hypotheses in a constant times log N queries, matching the information-theoretic query order; arbitrary instances need not satisfy those conditions.
relevance: Provides the strongest simple classical active-query control and the log-K signature a learned acquisition policy must beat in full cost rather than rediscover.
title: The Geometry of Generalized Binary Search

claims_supported: Adaptive submodularity formalizes diminishing returns for policies whose later selections depend on earlier observations.
For adaptive-submodular objectives, a simple adaptive greedy policy has competitiveness guarantees relative to the optimal policy, including active-learning version-space reduction applications.
relevance: Shows that sequential information-gain selection and strong greedy guarantees are classical; policy construction and version-space updates must be charged.
title: Adaptive Submodularity: A New Approach to Active Learning and Stochastic Optimization

claims_supported: The paper develops a Bayesian measure of the information supplied by an experiment using the expected change from prior to posterior uncertainty.
Selecting experiments by expected information therefore predates learned active-acquisition controllers and requires an explicit prior and likelihood model.
relevance: Establishes expected information gain as the classical Bayesian experimental-design baseline and exposes the cost of maintaining and scoring a belief model.
title: On a Measure of the Information Provided by an Experiment

claims_supported: Constructing a minimum-cost binary identification decision tree is NP-complete in the general test-set formulation.
An optimal decision-tree control can therefore be exact on the bounded benchmark while its construction cost and lack of general scalability must remain visible.
relevance: Prevents treating an exhaustively precomputed optimal acquisition tree as free or scalable and motivates reporting both probe depth and policy-build work.
title: Constructing Optimal Binary Decision Trees Is NP-Complete

claims_supported: The paper reframes active-learning example selection as reinforcement learning and explicitly trains a transferable data-selection policy.
Reported gains over heuristic active learning do not remove the simulation, policy-training, state representation or downstream classifier costs.
relevance: Direct prior art for a learned acquisition policy; the benchmark must compare it with exact and greedy classical controls while charging training and transfer failures.
title: Learning How to Active Learn: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach

claims_supported: Amortized inference scales latent-variable inference across large datasets by replacing per-datapoint optimization with a recognition network.
Inference error decomposes into approximation and amortization gaps, and imperfect recognition can dominate, so fast reuse does not make representation learning free.
relevance: Challenges a universal lower-bound reading while requiring the next benchmark to charge representation training and recognition error separately.
title: Inference Suboptimality in Variational Autoencoders

claims_supported: The information bottleneck seeks a short code for X that preserves information relevant to Y.
The objective yields self-consistent coding equations and an iterative solution, so the compression criterion and its optimization cost are explicit rather than free.
relevance: Provides a principled learned-compression candidate and a classical optimization control for decision-relevant predictive state.
title: The Information Bottleneck Method

claims_supported: A recurrent network trained by an outer reinforcement-learning algorithm can implement a distinct learned inner reinforcement-learning procedure in its dynamics.
Rapid adaptation exploits repeated structure in the training domain and follows substantial outer-loop training, so both the task-family prior and training workload belong in full-system accounting.
relevance: Shows a plausible route for strongly amortized adaptation and prevents treating every learned controller as only a static lookup table.
title: Learning to Reinforcement Learn

claims_supported: Costly-feature classification can be formulated as sequential decisions to purchase another feature or stop and classify.
A Double-DQN acquisition policy improved the reported precision-cost trade-off over specialized baselines on three datasets, while policy training and classifier inference remain system costs.
relevance: Directly challenges the narrow active-acquisition null and motivates evaluating learned value of information on non-handcrafted observations.
title: Classification with Costly Features Using Deep Reinforcement Learning

claims_supported: CSSR infers a minimal set of hidden Markovian causal states from discrete sequential data without fixing the number of states or transition architecture in advance.

Under its assumptions the inferred causal states are asymptotically reliable and form minimal sufficient statistics for prediction; finite-data history testing and state construction still incur cost.
relevance: Supplies the strongest non-neural classical control for learning predictive equivalence classes directly from raw histories.
title: Pattern Discovery in Time Series, Part I: Theory, Algorithm, Analysis, and Convergence

claims_supported: A statistically consistent spectral algorithm can learn a predictive-state representation directly from action-observation sequences.
The learned compact state supported approximate planning and a near-optimal policy in a high-dimensional vision-based robot task, while spectral estimation and planning remain charged work.
relevance: Makes spectral PSR the key classical learned-state comparator for the selected action-conditioned history benchmark.
title: Closing the Learning-Planning Loop with Predictive State Representations

claims_supported: Bisimulation semimetrics quantify behavioral similarity between finite-MDP states rather than requiring exact equivalence.
The metrics support state aggregation and bounds relating state distance to optimal values, but assume or estimate rewards and transitions and require metric computation.
relevance: Provides the exact behavioral-abstraction baseline and a testable link from representation error to decision quality.
title: Metrics for Finite Markov Decision Processes

claims_supported: Contrastive Predictive Coding learns latent representations by predicting future samples from an autoregressive context in latent space.

Its tractable contrastive objective uses negative sampling and demonstrated useful representations across speech, images, text and reinforcement learning, so encoder, context model and negatives must all be charged.
relevance: Provides a trainable predictive-representation candidate that does not receive state labels or a supplied symbolic partition.
title: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding

claims_supported: High-dimensional superposition supports item retrieval but crosstalk noise limits retrieval accuracy and information capacity.
The paper derives a unified retrieval analysis for several randomized connectionist representation models rather than assuming capacity is free.
relevance: Supplies the primary theoretical basis for testing VSA dimension-to-capacity scaling and false cleanup retrievals.
title: Theory of the superposition principle for randomized connectionist representations in neural networks

claims_supported: Circular convolution can encode compositional structures in fixed-width distributed vectors.
Recovered vectors are noisy and may require a separate associative cleanup memory.
relevance: Establishes binding, unbinding, and cleanup as distinct system components whose compute and state must all be charged.
title: Holographic Reduced Representations

claims_supported: Approximate nearest-neighbor data structures can trade polynomial space for sublinear query time in high-dimensional spaces.
Sublinear cleanup therefore has strong classical indexing controls and is not by itself evidence for a learned or VSA-specific mechanism.
relevance: Motivates an explicit classical routed-cleanup baseline and full space/query accounting.
title: Approximate nearest neighbors: towards removing the curse of dimensionality

claims_supported: Low-density parity-check codes use sparse parity constraints with iterative decoding rather than storing every valid word.
Sparse constraint decoding is established classical prior art for any energy interpretation of parity correction.
relevance: Supplies the direct classical factor-graph control for overlapping learned constraints.
title: Low-Density Parity-Check Codes

claims_supported: Expander codes admit linear-time sequential decoding and logarithmic-time parallel decoding with linear hardware.
Bit-flipping can monotonically reduce unsatisfied constraints under expansion assumptions, so parallel local correction is not uniquely energy-based.
relevance: Provides the strongest classical explanation for one-round or few-round overlapping parity relaxation.
title: Expander Codes

claims_supported: A neural decoder can generalize belief propagation by assigning weights to edges on a Tanner graph.
The reported symmetry lets the learned decoder train on a single codeword, demonstrating reuse while retaining belief propagation as the structural baseline.
relevance: Motivates learned-factor or learned-weight decoding while requiring comparison with the unlearned classical algorithm and full training cost.
title: Learning to Decode Linear Codes Using Deep Learning

claims_supported: Synchronous and asynchronous cellular update schedules can have different trajectories, cycles and basins even under the same local rule.
An asynchronous schedule is therefore a semantic design choice rather than a free optimization of a synchronous automaton.
relevance: Requires the new benchmark to match task semantics explicitly and to compare sparse event execution with both a synchronous sweep and an exact sequential finite-state control.
title: Synchronous and asynchronous updating in cellular automata

claims_supported: A learned embedding can make distances correspond to identity similarity, after which verification, recognition and clustering use standard metric-space methods.
Triplet training and mining are part of the representation-acquisition cost rather than free preprocessing.
relevance: Motivates the learned metric/hash candidate while requiring embedding fit and downstream lookup to be charged separately.
title: FaceNet: A Unified Embedding for Face Recognition and Clustering

claims_supported: SimCLR learns representations from paired augmented views with a contrastive objective.
Augmentation choice, nonlinear projection, batch size and training steps materially affect the learned representation and must not disappear from accounting.
relevance: Establishes paired-view contrastive learning as prior art and motivates a deliberately small analytic contrastive learner rather than claiming novelty.
title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

claims_supported: Probabilistic record linkage decides match, non-match or possible-link from comparison evidence under explicit error tradeoffs.
Entity binding from noisy records has a strong classical statistical control predating learned embeddings.
relevance: Supplies the full-scan probabilistic linkage baseline and prevents treating noisy-view identity binding as uniquely neural.
title: A Theory for Record Linkage

claims_supported: Explore-Compress-Compile jointly grows a DSL of reusable subroutines and a neural recognition model for program search.
Its evaluations learn domain-specific libraries for list functions, text editing and symbolic regression, so within-domain library discovery is established prior art rather than project novelty.
relevance: Requires any new HYP-0002 test to change domains or representations and to separate symbolic compression from learned search guidance.
title: Learning Libraries of Subroutines for Neurally-Guided Bayesian Program Induction

claims_supported: A hierarchical Bayesian prior can share statistical strength among programs for related tasks with few examples per task.
Combinatory structure provides a classical probabilistic account of reusable program fragments across tasks.
relevance: Supplies a non-neural multi-task transfer control and prevents attributing shared-library benefits solely to wake-sleep learning.
title: Learning Programs: A Hierarchical Bayesian Approach

claims_supported: Library learning modulo theory uses e-graphs, equality saturation and anti-unification to find reusable abstractions despite semantics-preserving syntactic variation.
The reported compression and speed gains establish a strong symbolic control for apparent cross-syntax abstraction.
relevance: A held-out-DSL test must compare against semantic normalization or anti-unification rather than treating renamed syntax as learned transfer.
title: babble: Learning Better Abstractions with E-Graphs and Anti-unification

claims_supported: Natural-language annotations can jointly guide program-library induction and search and can improve downstream synthesis even when test tasks have no language hints.
Language supervision supplies concept names and decomposition information, so its encoder and supervision are part of the system boundary.
relevance: Establishes language-grounded library learning while warning that a no-API Codex experiment must not hide semantic alignment in an external language model.
title: Leveraging Language to Learn Program Abstractions and Search Heuristics

claims_supported: LILO combines LLM-guided synthesis, Stitch-based symbolic compression and automatic documentation to learn richer libraries across three domains.
Its capability depends on an external pretrained language model, so model calls and language priors cannot be omitted from efficiency comparisons.
relevance: Marks the strongest nearby hybrid result but is not an admissible Codex-native candidate; it motivates a small explicit semantic-alignment control instead of an uncharged LLM teacher.
title: LILO: Learning Interpretable Libraries by Compressing and Documenting Code

claims_supported: Mamba uses input-dependent selective state-space parameters and a hardware-aware recurrent algorithm to obtain sequence processing linear in length.
Its language results make selective state-space models a necessary modern dense-sequence baseline rather than an unexplored successor principle.
relevance: Future claims about recurrent or state-space efficiency must compare capability and end-to-end cost against a modern selective SSM, not only a toy dense recurrent control.
title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

claims_supported: Byte Latent Transformer groups raw bytes into dynamically sized entropy-based patches and reports FLOP-controlled scaling at fixed inference cost.
Adaptive allocation of compute across input regions is therefore direct prior art for variable-granularity language processing.
relevance: A language-interface generation must charge byte encoding and adaptive segmentation and compare against dynamic patching before treating variable computation as novel.
title: Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens

claims_supported: Titans introduces a neural long-term memory module updated at test time and combines it with short-term attention in several architectures.
Its reported long-context evaluations make test-time learned memory a direct competitor for continual and experience-dependent inference claims.
relevance: HYP-0011 and continual-memory work must distinguish validated local compilation from modern test-time neural memorization and charge memory updates and retrieval.
title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

claims_supported: Product-key memory uses structured keys for fast exact nearest-neighbor access to very large learned memory layers.
The work explicitly studies increasing parameter capacity at nearly fixed active computation and is a direct capacity-versus-compute baseline.
relevance: Sparse-memory or knowledge-compute decoupling claims must include product-key retrieval, index construction, state and update costs as a strong neural baseline.
title: Large Memory Layers with Product Keys

claims_supported: Predictive state can be represented by multi-step action-conditional predictions grounded in observable data.
Any finite POMDP admits a linear PSR with no more core predictions than states in its minimal POMDP model.
relevance: Establishes the representational premise of HYP-0008 while separating existence of a compact PSR from the cost and identifiability of learning its core tests.
title: Predictive Representations of State

claims_supported: CSSR constructs recursive predictive states for discrete sequences and is asymptotically optimal under its structural assumptions.
Its reliability depends on data requirements and finite-history reconstruction rather than eliminating the coverage problem.
relevance: Makes CSSR a mandatory variable-memory classical control and prevents attributing causal-state reconstruction itself to a learned neural representation.
title: Blind Construction of Optimal Nonlinear Recursive Predictors for Discrete Sequences

claims_supported: A statistically consistent spectral algorithm can learn a transformed PSR directly from action-observation trajectories.
The learned predictive representation supported planning in a simulated high-dimensional vision task.
relevance: Supplies the strongest direct classical learned-state baseline for any high-dimensional PSR cohort and shows that vision-like observations alone do not create a distinct neural principle.
title: Closing the Learning-Planning Loop with Predictive State Representations

claims_supported: RPSP combines a predictive-state recursive filter with a reactive policy and supports continuous observations and actions.
Its filter is initialized by statistically consistent spectral/two-stage regression and then refined end-to-end by gradient optimization.
relevance: Shows that a fair learned RPSP is not independent of spectral PSR; a benchmark must isolate the value of end-task refinement rather than count shared initialization as a neural advantage.
title: Recurrent Predictive State Policy Networks

claims_supported: Non-uniform sampling can distort conditional probability estimates used by spectral PSR learning.
Matrix denoising and structural penalties can improve predictive performance under limited sampling of conditions.
relevance: Requires sparse-exploration tests to include coverage-aware spectral denoising rather than using an avoidably biased spectral estimator as a weak control.
title: Learning Predictive State Representations From Non-Uniform Sampling

claims_supported: Complete and consistent sum-product networks compute partition functions and marginals exactly in time linear in circuit size.
SPNs can be learned with backpropagation or EM and may compactly represent distributions for which ordinary graphical-model inference is difficult.
relevance: Establishes tractable probabilistic circuits as an existing but untested architectural family for compiled non-autoregressive uncertainty inference.
title: Sum-Product Networks: A New Deep Architecture

claims_supported: SPN structure can be learned recursively by discovering approximate variable independence and clustering related instances.
Learned SPNs can represent unbounded-treewidth distributions while retaining tractable inference, though worst-case structure learning and circuit size can be exponential.
relevance: Provides the direct structure-learning mechanism and warns that fit and circuit-size growth must be charged rather than treating tractability after compilation as free.
title: Learning the Structure of Sum-Product Networks

claims_supported: Smooth and decomposable probabilistic circuits support normalization, marginalization and conditioning in time linear in circuit size.
Einsum Networks vectorize circuit operations and report large practical learning and evaluation speedups without removing structural tractability constraints.
relevance: Supplies a modern implementation baseline and separates the circuit principle from inefficient sparse graph execution in future cost comparisons.
title: Einsum Networks: Fast and Scalable Learning of Tractable Probabilistic Circuits

claims_supported: Test-Time Training layers make the recurrent hidden state a machine-learning model and update it with a self-supervised learning step on the test sequence.
TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP retain linear sequence complexity, but the authors identify memory I/O as a remaining challenge for TTT-MLP.
relevance: Direct modern prior art for HYP-0014: a learned test-time state is established, so a local result must isolate the update law and charge every update, state access and memory movement.
title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States

claims_supported: Linearized self-attention is formally equivalent to fast-weight programming by additive outer-product updates.
A delta-rule update with learned rates addresses finite-memory overwrite and capacity limitations better than purely additive fast weights in the reported tasks.
relevance: Makes additive and delta-rule fast weights mandatory controls and prevents relabeling linear attention or online associative updates as a new mechanism.
title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers

claims_supported: Kernelized linear attention can be evaluated recurrently in linear sequence time by re-associating matrix products.
The recurrent formulation exposes linear attention as a state update rather than an intrinsically distinct non-recurrent architecture.
relevance: Supplies a strong recurrent-state control and requires separating benefits of learned online updates from the algebraic recurrence already present in linear attention.
title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention

claims_supported: Prediction by partial matching is an adaptive finite-context text-compression method that backs off when a longer context has insufficient evidence.
Its explicit escape and context-count machinery makes it a stronger classical null than a fixed-order n-gram.
relevance: Requires a PPM-style variable-order control before attributing held-out source compression to hierarchical reusable motifs.
title: Data Compression Using Adaptive Coding and Partial String Matching

claims_supported: Context-tree weighting efficiently mixes bounded-memory tree-source models rather than selecting one fixed context tree.
The method has explicit sequential coding, redundancy, compute and storage guarantees.
relevance: Makes context-tree weighting a mandatory universal-coding control and prevents a generic hierarchical mixture from being treated as novel by name alone.
title: The Context-Tree Weighting Method: Basic Properties

claims_supported: D3PM generalizes discrete diffusion with structured corruption kernels, including absorbing-mask transitions.
The paper reports discrete denoising results for both image and character-level text domains, establishing masked iterative generation as prior art rather than a new NEXTAI mechanism.
relevance: Supplies the direct discrete-sequence denoising precedent and requires charging every refinement round and corruption/training operation.
title: Structured Denoising Diffusion Models in Discrete State-Spaces

claims_supported: MaskGIT predicts masked tokens bidirectionally and iteratively refines many tokens in parallel instead of raster-order autoregressive decoding.
Its reported image-generation speedups demonstrate a critical-path advantage, while total model work and tokenization remain part of the system boundary.
relevance: Motivates a parallel-round versus total-work test and prevents treating masked iterative decoding itself as novel.
title: MaskGIT: Masked Generative Image Transformer

claims_supported: Levenshtein Transformer generates sequences through iterative insertion and deletion rather than a fixed left-to-right factorization.
Partially non-autoregressive editing is established for sequence generation, so any local result must compare quality, number of rounds and full edit work.
relevance: Provides a text-sequence iterative-editing baseline adjacent to masked denoising.
title: Levenshtein Transformer

claims_supported: MuZero combines tree search with a learned dynamics representation that predicts quantities relevant to planning without receiving environment dynamics.
Its capability still depends on repeated search, self-play data and model evaluation, which must all be charged in a full-system comparison.
relevance: Strong precedent for learned verifier/search guidance, but also evidence that search is not removed and is unsuitable for a tiny uncharged local quick.
title: Mastering Atari, Go, chess and shogi by planning with a learned model

claims_supported: S4 uses a structured state-space parameterization to model long sequences efficiently and reports strong results across multiple long-range benchmarks.
The work establishes efficient recurrent/convolutional sequence operators as modern baselines rather than evidence against autoregressive output dependence by themselves.
relevance: Requires any recurrent long-context direction to beat modern structured SSMs and to distinguish token-processing cost from sequential decoding depth.
title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

claims_supported: Hyena replaces attention with data-controlled long convolutions and reports subquadratic sequence mixing with competitive language modeling.
Its gains concern the sequence operator and hardware regime; generation can remain autoregressive, so operator speed alone does not answer the decoding-factorization question.
relevance: Makes long-convolution controls mandatory and helps reject another small SSM-versus-Transformer toy as low-information.
title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models

claims_supported: A neural statistician treats datasets rather than individual points as the represented objects and learns unsupervised dataset-level summary statistics.
The paper demonstrates dataset clustering, transfer of generative models and prediction for previously unseen classes.
relevance: Direct precedent for learning one family-blind representation of an unordered support set; it must be compared with simpler sufficient-statistic and set-pooling controls.
title: Towards a Neural Statistician

claims_supported: Conditional Neural Processes aggregate a context set into a task representation and condition predictions for new target inputs on that representation.
They are a direct learned meta-function baseline for few-observation transfer, not evidence that a particular summary is identifiable.
relevance: Makes a monolithic set-conditioned predictor mandatory when testing reusable task representations across unseen worlds.
title: Conditional Neural Processes

claims_supported: Modular meta-learning jointly learns reusable neural modules and task-specific structures that recombine those modules for new tasks.
Its BOUNCEGRAD procedure pays a structural search cost, which must be charged rather than treating module composition as free.
relevance: Direct precedent for learned module recombination and the strongest learned control for a future shared-mechanism composition test.
title: Modular meta-learning

claims_supported: Nonlinear blind source separation is generally non-identifiable from statistical independence alone.

Independent Mechanism Analysis introduces structural assumptions on independently chosen causal mechanisms to recover identifiability in settings where unconstrained nonlinear representations are ambiguous.
relevance: Requires a future shared-representation benchmark to state what mechanism variation makes the latent modules identifiable instead of assuming pooling will discover them.
title: Independent mechanism analysis, a new concept?

claims_supported: Slot Attention maps perceptual inputs to an exchangeable set of task-dependent slots through competitive iterative attention.
The reported slots support generalization to unseen object compositions, while relying on an architectural object-centric bias and downstream training objective.
relevance: Provides an object-centric learned decomposition precedent but warns that slot structure is an inductive bias whose fit and iterative attention costs must be charged.
title: Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention

claims_supported: Compositional generalization can be formulated as a property of the data-generating process rather than asserted from an architectural label.
The paper gives support and architecture conditions sufficient for compositional generalization and validates them empirically.
relevance: Directly motivates a pre-scoring support-coverage and identifiability gate for unseen combinations of shared mechanisms.
title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles

claims_supported: Object-centric compositional generalization is guaranteed only under explicit structural decoder assumptions and encoder-decoder consistency conditions.
Experiments on synthetic images support the practical relevance of those identifiability conditions.
relevance: Prevents treating exchangeable slots alone as sufficient evidence and requires semantic tests for recombination beyond clustering.
title: Provable Compositional Generalization for Object-Centric Learning

claims_supported: Deep Sets characterizes permutation-invariant set functions and provides a sum-pooling architecture for them.
Permutation invariance is a necessary baseline property for a learner whose support examples are an unordered set.
relevance: Supplies the simplest learned set-aggregation control and prevents attributing gains merely to permutation-invariant pooling.
title: Deep Sets

claims_supported: Set Transformer models interactions among set elements with permutation-invariant attention.
Inducing-point attention reduces its asymptotic set interaction cost from quadratic to linear in set size under the proposed construction.
relevance: Provides a stronger interaction-aware set encoder baseline and requires explicit attention/inducing-point work and state accounting.
title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks

claims_supported: SEQUITUR incrementally replaces repeated phrases with recursive grammar rules.
Its two grammar constraints permit linear time and space in the input length.
relevance: Direct classical control for any claim that incremental reusable nonterminal induction is novel or uniquely transferable.
title: Identifying Hierarchical Structure in Sequences: A Linear-Time Algorithm

claims_supported: Re-Pair is an off-line dictionary-based compressor that repeatedly substitutes frequent adjacent pairs.
The resulting dictionary is a straight-line grammar representation of the input.
relevance: Mandatory batch grammar/dictionary control for reusable repeated-fragment claims.
title: Off-line Dictionary-Based Compression

claims_supported: A grammar-based code transforms a finite string into a deterministic grammar that uniquely represents it and then encodes the grammar.
Under stated restrictions the codes are universal for finite-state sources; the presented construction batch-processes the complete string before grammar formation.
relevance: Defines the universal-code baseline and exposes future-byte leakage if a batch grammar is used for chronological prediction.
title: Grammar-Based Codes: A New Class of Universal Lossless Source Codes

claims_supported: A greedy sequential grammar transform constructs a sequence of irreducible grammars from which the source is recovered incrementally.
The associated universal lossless algorithms combine sequential grammar construction with arithmetic coding.
relevance: Shows that chronological grammar induction and coding are established controls rather than a distinct transfer mechanism.
title: Efficient Universal Lossless Data Compression Algorithms Based on a Greedy Sequential Grammar Transform—Part One: Without Context Models

claims_supported: Adaptor grammars generalize PCFGs with adaptors that induce dependencies among repeated uses.
Pitman-Yor adaptors express nonparametric Bayesian cached-subtree models and require a declared grammar plus inference procedure.
relevance: Strong probabilistic cached-grammar prior art; also identifies the ontology and inference-cost confounds for a raw-byte learner.
title: Adaptor Grammars: A Framework for Specifying Compositional Nonparametric Bayesian Models

claims_supported: General weighted automata can be learned by combining constrained completion of an incomplete Hankel matrix with spectral factorization.
The matrix-completion choice and spectral estimation are part of the learning algorithm and must be charged rather than treated as free representation discovery.
relevance: Direct classical prior art for the proposed generation-2 operator-completion learner and a mandatory explanation/control boundary.
title: Spectral Learning of General Weighted Automata via Constrained Matrix Completion

claims_supported: The Silverbox is an electronic implementation of a Duffing oscillator with a second-order linear dynamical system and a cubic static nonlinearity in feedback.
The authoritative benchmark download contains input V1, measured output V2, CSV copies and an additional Schroeder-phase multisine record.
relevance: Authoritative provenance and native input/output semantics for the proposed real system-identification transfer cohort; the page does not state dataset redistribution terms or a content digest.
title: Nonlinear Benchmark: Silverbox

claims_supported: DaISy is a publicly accessible system-identification database intended for reproducibility and comparison of identification methods.
The database provides gzip-compressed datasets and asks users to cite the database and specific dataset.
relevance: Authoritative provenance and use intent for the hair-dryer and robot-arm records; public availability and requested citation do not themselves establish redistribution rights.
title: DaISy: The Datasets

claims_supported: The hair-dryer record measures input voltage and output air temperature from a laboratory thermal process.
The published record contains 1000 samples in two columns.
relevance: Defines the native SISO prediction semantics and size of one proposed cohort member; it provides one trace and no official train/test split in the description.
title: DaISy 96-006: Hair dryer process description

claims_supported: The flexible robot-arm record studies transfer from measured reaction torque to arm acceleration under a periodic sine sweep.
The published record contains 1024 samples, with input torque in column one and output acceleration in column two.
relevance: Defines the native SISO prediction semantics and size of one proposed cohort member; it provides one trace and no official train/test split in the description.
title: DaISy 96-009: Flexible robot arm description

claims_supported: The official nonlinear-benchmarks loader exposes designated train/validation and test records for several benchmark datasets.
Its documentation warns that test data must not influence model decisions and documents Silverbox initialization and test subsets.
relevance: Authoritative split protocol for Silverbox and a potential source of future multi-trajectory cohorts; its software license does not establish redistribution rights for every underlying dataset.
title: Nonlinear Benchmarks data loader

claims_supported: The NanoDrone benchmark contains about 75000 real-flight samples with synchronized four-dimensional motor inputs and thirteen-dimensional state outputs.
It evaluates one-step and multi-step open-loop prediction and reserves the Melon trajectory type for test-time trajectory-level generalization.
relevance: Primary scientific specification for the proposed real multi-trajectory transfer screen and its system boundary.
title: Nonlinear System Identification Nano-drone Benchmark

claims_supported: The repository stores twelve training CSV trajectories: four runs each of Chirp, Random and Square.
The repository stores three Melon test CSV trajectories and documents a 100 Hz, 50-step evaluation horizon.
The audited root listing contains no LICENSE or COPYING file and the README states no explicit data-license identifier.
relevance: Authoritative artifact and split inventory. The absence of an explicit repository/data license blocks vendoring despite the paper describing the release as open-source.
title: Nano-Quadrotor System Identification Benchmark repository

claims_supported: NanoBench reports more than 170 flight trajectories spanning hover, excitation, tracking and aggressive maneuvers across multiple speed regimes.
It reports standardized train/test protocols for system identification, control and state-estimation tasks with synchronized actuator, state, estimator and controller signals.
relevance: Candidate for the next source-resolution gate because it may provide substantially more independent worlds than NanoDrone; repository identity and data license remain to be verified before use.
title: NanoBench: A Multi-Task Benchmark Dataset for Nano-Quadrotor System Identification, Control, and State Estimation

claims_supported: The NanoBench repository declares BSD-3-Clause coverage for its dataset and codebase and pins its current content through Git commit 0ae7d689749db174dc779ab2f7c416cc12e14e2b.
The README describes 170 recordings and a roughly 70/30 system-identification split, but states that the complete dataset will be deposited only after paper acceptance.

The authoritative commit tree contains 107 CSV paths representing 87 unique Git blob IDs; Task 1 is an unresolved gitlink without a submodule URL or .gitmodules mapping, so its documented split implementation is unavailable.
relevance: Authoritative artifact, license and reproducibility audit for the proposed NanoBench transfer cohort; establishes that the current release is incomplete and cannot freeze the claimed evaluator.
title: NanoBench IROS 2026 repository at commit 0ae7d689

claims_supported: DronePropA reports 130 real indoor flight logs spanning propeller-defect conditions.
The associated files are declared under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.
relevance: Concrete next candidate for a same-interface, multi-condition real dynamics cohort with explicit rights; provenance, hashes, condition factoriality and held-out split still require a separate gate.
title: DronePropA: Motion trajectories dataset for defective drones

claims_supported: The corpus contains 130 MAT files: 26 flights for each of five trajectories.
Drone 1 covers every three-fault-type by three-severity by two-speed combination; two additional drones contribute healthy maximum-speed references only.
The common 1 kHz schema includes state, IMU, thrust, motor, ESC, battery and flight-mode signals.
relevance: Primary experimental and schema specification establishing the possible factor-recombination split and the single-airframe fault limitation.
title: DronePropA: Motion trajectories dataset for defective drones

claims_supported: The immutable dataset release is registered as DOI 10.17632/ftdyxrr3c5.1 and was published on 2024-12-17.
The registry declares CC BY 4.0 rights but exposes no file sizes, formats or content digests in its DOI metadata.
relevance: Version and rights identity for a future bounded acquisition; local archive and extracted-file hashes remain mandatory.
title: DataCite record for DronePropA version 1

claims_supported: Published Mendeley datasets are permanent unchanging public records identified by dataset ID and version.
The public DronePropA interface exposes a version-1 Download All endpoint for the 4.13 GB release.
relevance: Authoritative acquisition and immutability contract used to retrieve and locally hash the exact version-1 archive without credentials.
title: Mendeley Datasets API quick start and DronePropA public download

claims_supported: The official C-MAPSS release contains four same-schema train/test trajectory groups with 708 training engines and 708 test engines in total.
FD001/FD002 contain one HPC fault mode under one/six operating conditions; FD003/FD004 contain HPC and fan degradation under one/six conditions.
The release is public-access, but both the dataset and ZIP resource explicitly state License not specified; CKAN publishes no resource size, content hash or last-modified value.
relevance: Authoritative provenance, structure, access and rights metadata for the rejected no-download classic C-MAPSS cohort.
title: CMAPSS Jet Engine Simulated Data

claims_supported: The PHM08 data were generated from C-MAPSS by imposing randomized gradual degradation until a failure criterion was reached.
Training trajectories run to failure, while test trajectories are censored before failure for remaining-useful-life evaluation.
relevance: Primary methodological provenance for what the classic C-MAPSS trajectories and targets can identify scientifically.
title: Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Prognostics

claims_supported: The newer N-CMAPSS dataset is explicitly declared CC0 1.0 and provides run-to-failure trajectories, health and fault classes under real flight-condition profiles.
Its DS02 subset supplies six development engines and three independently held-out test engines with common scenario, sensor, virtual-sensor and health-parameter fields.
relevance: A stronger explicitly licensed successor source for the next no-download artifact and identifiability gate.
title: Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Dataset under Real Flight Conditions for Prognostics and Diagnostics

claims_supported: NASA's official Prognostics Data Repository lists Turbofan Engine Degradation Simulation-2 as dataset 17, provided by NASA PCoE with ETH Zurich and PARC.
The official download target is the phm-datasets S3 archive named 17. Turbofan Engine Degradation Simulation Data Set 2.zip.
relevance: Authoritative artifact provenance and acquisition endpoint for the N-CMAPSS DS02 pre-download gate.
title: Prognostics Center of Excellence Data Set Repository

claims_supported: The community loader documents DS08a-009 units 1 through 9 as development and 10 through 15 as test.
It treats the official HDF5 files as already split and warns that their full-resolution size requires memory-aware loading.
relevance: Secondary split metadata used only to decide whether extracting the exact official DS08a member is worth a real-file audit; the split and flight-class counts must be reverified from the authoritative HDF5 before any evaluator decision.
title: N-CMAPSS_DL dataset split documentation

claims_supported: Prediction-with-expert-advice methods aggregate functional forecasts by updating expert weights rather than transferring the experts' internal parameters.

Long-horizon forecast aggregation is established prior art, so a positive NEXTAI result would concern cross-family transfer under this frozen costed contract rather than novelty of convex expert mixing.
relevance: Direct prior art for the proposed convex mixture over persistence, ridge ARX and RLS; it prevents treating exponential or convex reweighting itself as a new computational principle.
title: Mixing Past Predictions

claims_supported: Jointly training all tasks can reduce accuracy when objectives compete, so one shared model is not a neutral default.
Empirically learned task grouping can improve the time-accuracy trade-off relative to both one monolithic multi-task network and fully separate networks.
relevance: Explains why shared-versus-independent and cross-family-only contrasts are mandatory; task grouping itself cannot be imported into NEXTAI for free because it uses task identities and incurs search/training cost.
title: Which Tasks Should Be Learned Together in Multi-task Learning?

claims_supported: Multi-task optimization can suffer detrimental interference when task gradients conflict under specific curvature and magnitude conditions.
Projecting conflicting task gradients improved efficiency and performance in the reported supervised and reinforcement-learning settings.
relevance: Provides a credible optimization-level explanation for negative pooled transfer, but its task-separated gradients require task identity and therefore do not rescue a family-blind learner under the frozen NEXTAI interface.
title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning

claims_supported: Transfer relationships between visual tasks are directional and non-trivial rather than implied by human semantic intuition.
The reported task taxonomy is computed from measured representation transfers and an optimization over candidate transfer policies.
relevance: Supports observationally learned affinity rather than a hand ontology, while making clear that exhaustive affinity estimation and task labels are part of the charged system boundary and are unavailable to the current anonymous cross-family learner.
title: Taskonomy: Disentangling Task Transfer Learning

claims_supported: Successor features factor a value function into environment dynamics and a task-dependent reward representation.
The transfer guarantees and experiments address tasks whose reward changes while the environment dynamics remain shared.
relevance: Shows a valid reusable-representation route under an explicit shared-dynamics assumption; the heterogeneous NEXTAI families do not receive that assumption, so positive transfer must be empirically identified rather than presumed.
title: Successor Features for Transfer in Reinforcement Learning

claims_supported: Universal successor-feature approximators combine a task-conditioned function approximator with successor features and generalized policy improvement.
Their reported unseen-task generalization explicitly conditions the approximator on a task description.
relevance: A strong transfer precedent that also exposes a forbidden shortcut for NEXTAI: an evaluator-supplied task or family descriptor cannot substitute for a representation learned solely from anonymous public observations.
title: Universal Successor Features Approximators

claims_supported: DeepMDP trains a latent model by predicting rewards and the distribution over next latent states.
The paper connects small latent reward and transition losses to approximate bisimulation and value-function quality.
relevance: Constrains the meaning of predictive equivalence: a compressed key is useful only to the extent that its frozen self-supervised targets preserve the future quantities needed by the downstream query, not merely because it clusters observations.
title: DeepMDP: Learning Continuous Latent Space Models for Representation Learning

claims_supported: Causal Chambers are computer-controlled real physical systems designed for manipulations and measurements rather than simulations.
The project publishes time-series and interventional datasets with open hardware, software and ground-truth causal models.
relevance: Primary scientific provenance that the selected wind-tunnel source is a physical intervention testbed; the authors explicitly warn that it is a sanity check whose success need not transfer to more complex systems.
title: Causal chambers as a real-world physical testbed for AI methodology

claims_supported: wt_changepoints_v1 repeatedly changes one actuator at random within each experiment and marks the first measurement after each change.
The dataset has ten load_in_seed experiments, direct ZIP distribution with MD5 7e9f26d192674f2aaa6481f4415007eb, and CC BY 4.0 data licensing.
relevance: Authoritative dataset description, download identity and license for the only source passing the cycle-114 source gate.
title: Causal Chamber dataset: wt_changepoints_v1

claims_supported: The frozen generator creates seeds 0 through 9, ten interventions per seed, and 100 to 300 measurements per intervention.
The manipulated load_in level is sampled from four values: 0.01, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5.
relevance: Exact acquisition-gate evidence for recurrence and at least three potential perturbation scales; actual CSV realization remains to be verified locally before task design.
title: wt_changepoints_v1 load_in experiment generator

claims_supported: SKAB v0.9 is a real multivariate water-circulation testbed corpus with anomaly and changepoint annotations.
Each CSV is a separate experiment containing a single anomaly, while directories encode valve1, valve2 or other experiment categories.
relevance: Primary repository evidence rejecting SKAB for the exact within-trajectory recurrent-intervention contract; cross-file category joins would reintroduce semantic routing.
title: Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark (SKAB)

authors: iTrust, Singapore University of Technology and Design
claims_supported: SWaT A1 records 11 days of continuous operation, 51 sensors and actuators, and 41 attacks during four attack days on a physical water-treatment testbed.
