The official dataset page provides access through a request workflow rather than a direct frozen public archive.
relevance: Primary source showing strong recurrent physical perturbation content but insufficient open acquisition provenance for the exact NEXTAI gate.
title: Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) dataset characteristics

authors: iTrust, Singapore University of Technology and Design
claims_supported: Receiving SWaT requires a request and agreement to attribution and notification terms.
Recipients may not share the dataset in either private or public settings; every additional recipient must submit a separate request.
relevance: Primary access-policy evidence rejecting SWaT for a reproducible repository-owned acquisition/freeze cycle despite its scientifically relevant trajectories.
title: iTrust dataset terms of usage

claims_supported: Dynamic mode decomposition with control learns a data-driven state-transition model that separates process dynamics from actuation using observed snapshots and inputs.
relevance: Direct classical prior art for a learned recurrent transition operator with an observed control; any positive NEXTAI result must be framed as efficiency evidence, not architectural novelty.
title: Dynamic Mode Decomposition with Control

claims_supported: Meta-AF explicitly learns online adaptive-filter update rules from data and compares them with hand-derived LMS and RLS-style adaptive filtering.
relevance: Direct prior art limiting novelty of learned local update laws and motivating strong LMS/RLS controls plus full update-cost accounting.
title: Meta-AF: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Filters

claims_supported: Unsupervised disentanglement is not identifiable without inductive biases on the model and data.
The authors' large empirical study did not find that more disentanglement reliably reduced downstream sample complexity.
relevance: Supports treating repeated anonymous cross-family failures as an identifiability warning rather than a request for another representation parameterization.
title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations

claims_supported: Non-i.i.d. observation pairs sharing at least one latent factor can supply enough weak structure for identifiable disentanglement under the paper's assumptions.
The practical method does not require labels naming the shared or changed factors.
relevance: Identifies observation pairing as a possible ontology-free symmetry breaker, but only when the required shared-factor pair structure is actually present and auditable.
title: Weakly-Supervised Disentanglement Without Compromises

claims_supported: Generic nonlinear ICA from i.i.d. observations is unidentifiable.
Conditional independence given an auxiliary variable can make nonlinear components identifiable and can be estimated by generalized contrastive learning.
relevance: Defines a concrete identifiability gate: a proposed shared representation must name an observable auxiliary variable and verify the required variation instead of assuming canonical coordinates emerge.
title: Nonlinear ICA Using Auxiliary Variables and Generalized Contrastive Learning

claims_supported: Interventional data can provide geometric support signatures that identify latent causal factors under explicit perfect or imperfect intervention conditions.
The paper obtains identification only under stated assumptions on interventions, support geometry and the observation map.
relevance: Shows a principled route beyond observational ambiguity while preventing NEXTAI from treating arbitrary controls or regime changes as sufficient causal supervision.
title: Interventional Causal Representation Learning

claims_supported: Causal representation learning is severely ill-posed without additional structure.
The paper proves identifiability under a suitable grouping assumption on observational variables and proposes a consistent self-supervised estimator.
relevance: Grouping is a possible alternative symmetry breaker, but using evaluator-supplied channel groups would be hidden ontology unless the grouping is mechanically observable and source-identical.
title: Causal Representation Learning Made Identifiable by Grouping of Observational Variables

claims_supported: Linearized self-attention is formally equivalent to fast-weight programming with additive outer-product updates.
A delta-rule fast-weight update can correct stored key-value mappings and can use learned update rates.
relevance: Makes fast-weight memory a direct classical/neural-update relative of already tested NEXTAI update and memory families, requiring an explicit discriminator rather than a renamed recurrence.
title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers

claims_supported: Test-Time Training layers treat the hidden state as a model updated by a self-supervised gradient step on the test sequence.
TTT-Linear contains a construction exactly equivalent to linear attention, while larger TTT variants add learned views, normalization, residual structure and inner optimization.
relevance: A scaled TTT system is important external evidence, but a tiny local reimplementation would collapse to mechanisms already tested against LMS, RLS and recurrent controls rather than isolate a new principle.
title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States

claims_supported: Titans updates a neural long-term memory at test time using gradient-based surprise, momentum and forgetting.
The reported architecture combines learned memory with persistent parameters and, in some variants, sliding-window attention.
relevance: Surprise-gated deep memory is a distinct scaled architecture, but current NEXTAI cohorts cannot isolate it from update-law, recurrent-state and routing effects at matched capability without recreating a large neural system.
title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

claims_supported: PonderNet learns a distribution over computation steps and optimizes an explicit prediction-quality versus computation trade-off.
The paper evaluates extrapolation and reports adaptive computation on synthetic reasoning and question-answering tasks.
relevance: Defines the learned-halting alternative that must add predictive information beyond a cheap transition residual or convergence certificate before HYP-0004 can be revived.
title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder

claims_supported: Deep equilibrium models represent the limit of a weight-tied transformation by directly solving for a fixed point.
The fixed-point formulation provides constant-memory effective depth while retaining iterative root-finding computation.
relevance: Provides the matched classical-style convergence/fixed-point account: learned halting is not distinct when a residual or root-finding certificate already determines adequate stopping.
title: Deep Equilibrium Models

claims_supported: ATLAS optimizes long-term memory against current and past tokens rather than only the latest input.
The reported DeepTransformer family increases memory capacity and management together and is evaluated as a scaled Transformer-like system.
relevance: A bounded local version would not isolate a new principle from replay, test-time optimization and recurrent memory already controlled in NEXTAI; the scaled system is outside current matched local cohorts.
title: ATLAS: Learning to Optimally Memorize the Context at Test Time

claims_supported: A predictive Markov blanket representation can remain underspecified for multi-source domain adaptation.
The paper's identifiability result requires partitioning the label Markov blanket into parents, children and spouses.
relevance: The required causal-role partition is not candidate-visible in the anonymous frozen NEXTAI cohorts; adding it manually would be a forbidden ontology rather than learned transfer.
title: A General Representation-Based Approach to Multi-Source Domain Adaptation

claims_supported: The theory links emergence of algebraic symbolic structure to geometric constraints including group invariance.
Its data-scaling account depends on the task's group invariance rather than generic parameter sharing.
relevance: Channel-permutation equivariance in v7 is an anonymization symmetry, not evidence of a shared task algebra; previous equivariant learners failed foreign-family transfer.
title: Why Neural Networks Can Discover Symbolic Structures with Gradient-based Training: An Algebraic and Geometric Foundation for Neurosymbolic Reasoning

claims_supported: Compositional transfer across observation and action spaces is obtained with specialized differentiable interface modules and a shared controller.
Novel modalities are integrated by adapting their specialized encoding modules.
relevance: The specialized interfaces rely on modality-specific structure and violate the current source-identical family-blind learner constraint, so they are not a clean test in v7.
title: Compositional Interfaces for Compositional Generalization

claims_supported: The public benchmark evaluates causal representation learning on a controlled real optical system with known causal inputs.
Representative CRL methods fail on the real system and several already fail on a simplified synthetic ablation, motivating a real-world sanity check.
relevance: The associated lt_crl_benchmark_v1 may provide synchronized images, natural interventions and ground-truth factors missing from current cohorts, but its candidate-visible contract and ontology boundary require a no-scoring audit before any migration.
title: Sanity Checking Causal Representation Learning on a Simple Real-World System

claims_supported: lt_crl_benchmark_v1 synchronizes 64-pixel images and sensor rows with five actuator factors across observational, single-intervention, temporal and uniform protocols.
The public archive is CC BY 4.0, has MD5 8ec492afffd0142abd70b1fa7082b104, and was 2763884276 bytes according to an HTTP HEAD request.
relevance: Defines the immutable public data contract and storage boundary audited before any NEXTAI migration; no archive contents were downloaded.
title: Causal Chamber dataset: lt_crl_benchmark_v1

claims_supported: The official CCRL and multiview evaluations split samples 80/10/10 while retaining the same environment proportions, rather than holding out environments.
The official multiview setup uses hand-defined sensor/image views and ground-truth content selection during training; CITRIS uses one temporal process split into consecutive 80K/10K/10K segments.
relevance: Shows that the published implementation is a factor-recovery sanity check on one physical mixing system, not a frozen transfer test over unseen worlds with a source-identical interface.
title: CRLSanityCheck official implementation

claims_supported: The inspected catalog provides Light Tunnel standard, Wind Tunnel standard and Wind Tunnel pressure-control configurations, with lt_walks_v1 and lt_interventions_standard_v1 sharing the same Light Tunnel configuration.
The Light and Wind Tunnel signal columns are disjoint apart from generic metadata; wt_pressure_control_v1 adds PID-specific state and contains one 10K hatch_0 experiment.
relevance: Defines the cross-system public metadata boundary used to reject a common anonymous numeric transfer contract without downloading any archive bodies.
title: Causal Chamber cross-system numeric dataset catalog

claims_supported: CausalBench uses two biological contexts, the RPE1 and K562 cell lines.
Its regimes vary observational and partial/full interventional training data within those datasets.
relevance: The explicit two-context boundary rejects CausalBench for a three-context unseen-world transfer contract before data acquisition.
title: A large-scale benchmark for network inference from single-cell perturbation data

claims_supported: sci-Plex 3 screened A549, K562 and MCF7 against 188 compounds at four doses in duplicate.
The release contains about 650000 transcriptomes and is public as GEO GSE139944, whose supplementary archive is listed as 9.2 GB.
relevance: The coherent but exactly three-context design cannot reserve an unseen context and still provide three genuine source-context scales.
title: Massively multiplex chemical transcriptomics at single-cell resolution

claims_supported: After QC Tahoe-100M contains 47 sufficiently covered cell lines, 379 drugs, 1135 drug-dose combinations and 52886 unique cell-line-drug-dose conditions.
The experiment includes plate-matched DMSO controls and a biological replicate plate.
relevance: Establishes enough recorded context and perturbation breadth to justify a metadata-only local feasibility audit, not migration or scoring.
title: Tahoe-100M: A Giga-Scale Single-Cell Perturbation Atlas for Context-Dependent Gene Function and Cellular Modeling

claims_supported: The hosted expression table stores raw sparse counts with stable integer gene token IDs, cell-line IDs, sample IDs, plate IDs and DMSO control labels.
At commit 2dc57900b7981cfcf5e211527169a0b006546a95 the hosting page reports CC0-1.0, streaming access and a 429 GB total artifact.
relevance: Defines the pinned public artifact, mechanical coordinate interface and acquisition boundary that a later feasibility audit must verify without using curated biological annotations.
title: Tahoe-100M public dataset artifact

claims_supported: The official alternative Tahoe-100M distribution contains 1344 samples and 100648790 cells in h5ad count matrices with Parquet metadata.

At repository commit 4f7bb170c61d2fafce70f67db6e52c7d9af1be4b the recommended Google Marketplace bucket is Requester Pays, the deprecated bucket has an end date, and the data are organized by experimental plates rather than per cell line.
relevance: Confirms that the alternative official host does not provide a free, context-partitioned local acquisition path and would require cloud billing/credentials plus cross-plate filtering.
title: Arc Virtual Cell Atlas Tahoe-100M data access

claims_supported: The Forward-Forward algorithm replaces a conventional forward/backward training pass with separate positive and negative forward passes.

Each hidden layer uses its own goodness objective, so training need not propagate derivatives through later layers; the paper presents preliminary results rather than a demonstrated full-system scaling advantage.
relevance: Defines the selected, already-known layer-local credit-assignment mechanism and prevents NEXTAI from claiming novelty; a scout must charge negative generation, every layer-local update, label scoring, state and full inference work.
title: The Forward-Forward Algorithm: Some Preliminary Investigations

claims_supported: Equilibrium propagation trains an energy-based recurrent network through free and target-nudged phases using the same dynamical circuit.
The update corresponds to a well-defined objective gradient but requires iterative relaxation and symmetric energy dynamics.
relevance: Provides the strongest nearby two-phase local-learning alternative; it is not selected for the first scout because relaxation depth and energy inference would change several causal factors and revisit the already tested energy family.
title: Equilibrium Propagation: Bridging the Gap between Energy-Based Models and Backpropagation

claims_supported: Feedback alignment can train multilayer networks using fixed random feedback weights instead of exact transposes of forward weights.
It still transmits a downstream error signal through a reverse pathway, so it relaxes weight transport rather than eliminating cross-layer error communication.
relevance: Supplies a matched alternative credit-assignment control and explains why the breadth scout selects the more causally distinct no-backward-pass Forward-Forward rule first.
title: Random synaptic feedback weights support error backpropagation for deep learning

claims_supported: A multiresolution approximation can be represented by nested approximation spaces and an orthonormal wavelet decomposition.
The fast pyramidal transform supplies a local hierarchical analysis and reconstruction algorithm.
relevance: Classical basis for the frozen dyadic Haar representation; NEXTAI claims no novelty for multiresolution analysis.
title: A theory for multiresolution signal decomposition: the wavelet representation

claims_supported: The lifting scheme constructs wavelet transforms through local predict and update steps.
Lifting supports in-place multiscale transforms and motivates testing learned local operators separately from a fixed transform.
relevance: Direct prior art for local lifting operators; the scout tests a narrow learned forecasting operator in a frozen Haar coordinate system, not a novel wavelet construction.
title: The lifting scheme: A construction of second generation wavelets

claims_supported: Growing Neural Gas incrementally adds prototypes from local accumulated error and learns their neighborhood topology.
Its representation and search state grow with discovered units unless capacity and lookup are explicitly bounded.
relevance: Shows that a growing event/operator dictionary is established prior art and would largely repeat NEXTAI routing, indexing and transition-bank tests rather than supply a fundamentally new mechanism.
title: A Growing Neural Gas Network Learns Topologies

claims_supported: Adaptive Resonance Theory incrementally forms stable recognition categories for arbitrary input sequences.
A match-or-reset mechanism decides whether an existing category may learn or a new category search is required.
relevance: Supplies the strongest established category-creation alternative to an operator dictionary and requires a matched bounded-category control rather than novelty credit.
title: Adaptive Resonance Theory: Stable Self-Organization of Neural Recognition Codes in Response to Arbitrary Lists of Input Patterns

claims_supported: Predictive state represents dynamical state through multi-step action-conditional predictions of future observations.
A linear predictive state representation can be no larger than a minimal POMDP state model under the paper's assumptions.
relevance: Future-grounded state discovery is direct prior art; any NEXTAI learned operator state must beat PSR-style or exact predictive-state controls at full acquisition and update cost.
title: Predictive Representations of State

claims_supported: E-prop factors recurrent-network learning into neuron-local eligibility traces and broadcast learning signals for online updates.
The method approaches BPTT on reported tasks but still requires recurrent state, eligibility storage and a learning-signal pathway.
relevance: Defines a strong local-plasticity alternative and prevents treating locality alone as novelty; a scout must charge eligibility state and compare against LMS/RLS and recurrence-disabled controls.
title: A solution to the learning dilemma for recurrent networks of spiking neurons

claims_supported: A timing-dependent local plasticity model can reduce postsynaptic latency for recurring predictive spike patterns.
The reported efficiency concerns spike timing and prediction coding rather than demonstrated full-system capability-per-cost scaling.
relevance: Supports testing a surprise-triggered local predictive-plasticity principle while requiring explicit event encoding, idle maintenance, update traffic and matched-quality accounting.
title: Spiking time-dependent plasticity leads to efficient coding of predictions

claims_supported: Uniform matrix product states support sequence-level parallel evaluation with logarithmic contraction depth.
The probabilistic tensor-network formulation supports conditional sequence generation.
relevance: Direct prior art for the selected parallel conditional-inference mechanism; NEXTAI must test capability per full cost rather than claim tensor-network novelty.
title: Tensor Networks for Probabilistic Sequence Modeling

claims_supported: Weighted finite automata, observable operator models and predictive state representations have closely related finite-dimensional sequence semantics.
Equivalent model classes can differ in parameterization without supplying a distinct computational principle.
relevance: Prevents treating an ordinary sequential MPS sequence model as orthogonal to prior WFA/OOM/PSR failures; v4 isolates only the parallel contraction property.
title: Links Between Multiplicity Automata, Observable Operator Models and Predictive State Representations: a Unified Learning Framework

claims_supported: Randomly initialized matrix product states can fail to capture nonlocal correlations during gradient training.
Initialization and training dynamics are a concrete failure alternative for tensor-network learners.
relevance: Requires frozen initialization and a no-post-score-tuning rule so a negative scout is not rescued after observing results.
title: Matrix Product State Training: Causality Trap and How to Avoid It

claims_supported: Imitation learning can learn adaptive node-ordering policies for branch-and-bound over a family of optimization problems.
A learned order can improve anytime search performance without replacing the underlying exact branch-and-bound method.
relevance: Direct prior art for learned exact-search ordering; EXP-0036 therefore tests end-to-end amortization and source-identical controls rather than novelty of learned ordering.
title: Learning to Search in Branch and Bound Algorithms

claims_supported: A learned ranking surrogate can imitate expensive strong branching for variable selection.
Reducing search-tree nodes is not sufficient by itself because strong branching and learned ranking have different per-node and acquisition costs.
relevance: Supports NEXTAI's requirement to charge fit, state and repeated query work instead of treating a smaller exact-search tree as an end-to-end win.
title: Learning to Branch in Mixed Integer Programming

claims_supported: A graph neural branching policy trained by imitation can generalize from smaller to significantly larger optimization instances.
The learned policy preserves an exact branch-and-bound solver while changing its variable-selection heuristic.
relevance: Shows that out-of-scale transfer is possible for learned branching, but EXP-0036's negative remains specific to its priority statistics and declared R1/R4/R16 cost boundary.
title: Exact Combinatorial Optimization with Graph Convolutional Neural Networks

claims_supported: In a visibly pushdown automaton the input symbol determines whether the machine pushes, pops or leaves the stack unchanged.
Visibly pushdown languages retain robust closure and decision properties while expressing nested call-return structure.
relevance: The seven-symbol call/return/internal structure learned in EXP-0042 is computationally a small visibly pushdown language; stack-mediated unseen-depth execution is established theory rather than a new automaton class.
title: Visibly Pushdown Languages

claims_supported: A recurrent controller coupled to a trainable stack can learn basic algorithmic sequence patterns.
Structured expandable memory can supply capabilities that ordinary fixed-state recurrent models lack.
relevance: Direct prior art for learning stack operations from sequential examples; EXP-0042 differs in exhaustive discrete role induction, anonymous symbols, masked closure prediction and audited full-cost controls, not in the stack principle.
title: Inferring Algorithmic Patterns with Stack-Augmented Recurrent Nets

claims_supported: Training on bounded nesting and testing closing-symbol prediction at deeper nesting is an established probe of recursion generalization.
Explicit stack-based models can approach perfect accuracy on generalized Dyck tasks, while standard recurrent models are less reliable.
relevance: The central depth-extrapolation signature and closure-symbol task of EXP-0042 have close prior art; robustness, hidden role induction and end-to-end cost are the remaining differentiators.
title: Can Recurrent Neural Networks Learn Nested Recursion?

claims_supported: Small LSTMs can emulate counters on Dyck-1 and shuffle languages.
The tested ordinary recurrent networks did not learn Dyck-2 well, where recognition requires stack-like memory rather than only counting.
relevance: Supports the finite-state/counter versus typed-stack discrimination used by the source-identical ablations, but prevents treating that separation itself as novel.
title: LSTM Networks Can Perform Dynamic Counting

claims_supported: Attention-based sequence models can look successful on a closing-bracket tagging metric yet fail exact deeper completion.
The authors conclude that a commonly used Dyck task is insufficient by itself to establish understanding of a context-free grammar.
relevance: Justifies retaining exact whole-closure prediction and adding a recoverable-corruption adversarial variant before assigning broader mechanism confidence.
title: Learning the Dyck Language with Attention-based Seq2Seq Models

claims_supported: V-Star infers visibly pushdown grammars and nesting structure from program-input samples.
Its active-learning procedure adapts exact automata-learning ideas to practical nested formats including JSON, XML and S-expressions.
relevance: Shows that observation-driven identification of call/return structure is an active grammatical-inference direction; EXP-0042 is a smaller passive finite-alphabet case and cannot claim the general inference novelty.
title: V-Star: Learning Visibly Pushdown Grammars from Program Inputs

claims_supported: The official cu124 package index publishes a Windows CPython 3.13 wheel for torch 2.6.0.
The installed local runtime can therefore be pinned without an external model service.
relevance: Pins the exact local-only learner runtime used by the learned discrete addressing cohort.
title: PyTorch cu124 package index

claims_supported: CUDA 12.4 Update 1 lists Windows driver 551.78 as the corresponding toolkit driver version.
relevance: Documents compatibility of the local RTX 4070 driver 551.78 with the pinned torch 2.6.0+cu124 runtime; this is infrastructure evidence, not scientific evidence.
title: CUDA Toolkit 12.4 Update 1 Release Notes

claims_supported: Classical index structures can be viewed as models mapping keys to record positions or existence.
Recursive model indexes use learned hierarchy but their benefit depends on the key distribution and full system costs.
relevance: A learned hierarchy over supplied sortable keys is established prior art and is not by itself a learned representation result; NEXTAI must withhold IDs/keys and charge representation, routing, update and fallback.
title: The Case for Learned Index Structures

claims_supported: A deep representation can be trained by back-propagating through a differentiable boundary-tree approximation.
The learned representation is coupled to nearest-neighbour tree traversal.
relevance: Direct prior art for jointly learning a representation and tree-based nearest-neighbour routing; a NEXTAI tree test can be a controlled replication under raw anonymous views and full-cost scaling, not a novelty claim.
title: Learning Deep Nearest Neighbor Representations Using Differentiable Boundary Trees

claims_supported: Adaptive neural trees learn representations, routing functions and leaf predictors jointly.
Conditional tree traversal can provide lightweight hierarchical inference.
relevance: Shows that learned hierarchical conditional routing is an established mechanism; the discriminating NEXTAI question is matched-quality access scaling and local insertion, not whether such trees can be trained.
title: Adaptive Neural Trees

claims_supported: Sparse differentiable tree activations can route samples through only a small portion of a tree.
Specialized sparse forward and backward algorithms realize conditional computation rather than evaluating every node.
relevance: Prevents counting dense soft-tree evaluation as sublinear routing and motivates an explicit visited-node and bytes-touched audit in any hierarchical successor.
title: The Tree Ensemble Layer: Differentiability meets Conditional Computation

claims_supported: Similarity-graph nearest-neighbour search can fail in local minima.
Learned vertex representations can improve greedy routing by encoding global graph structure.
relevance: A distinct graph-routing alternative already exists, but its global representation acquisition and index-update costs must be charged; it should not be mixed with a tree quick or treated as evidence before official harness reproduction.
title: Learning to Route in Similarity Graphs

claims_supported: Set Transformer provides permutation-invariant set processing with attention.
Inducing-point attention reduces the quadratic self-attention cost to a form linear in set size for a fixed number of inducing points.
relevance: Establishes that permutation-invariant inducing-point attention is prior art. NEXTAI's discriminating question is instead whether one source-identical learner transfers across frozen worlds at matched quality and full end-to-end cost.
title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks

claims_supported: Product-key memories factor keys into subkeys to address a large memory efficiently.
Structured key lookup can expose a large learned memory without scoring every slot densely.
relevance: Provides prior art for structured sparse learned memory. Any NEXTAI use must charge key construction, lookup, memory traffic, update and fallback and cannot claim novelty from factorized addressing alone.
title: Large Memory Layers with Product Keys

claims_supported: Routing Transformer uses online clustering to sparsify attention.
Its routing mechanism targets lower asymptotic attention cost than dense quadratic attention.
relevance: Shows learned sparse routing is established rather than a NEXTAI novelty claim. The proposed screen must compare learned routing to frozen routing and dense source-identical attention under matched quality and full accounting.
title: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers

claims_supported: Pattern databases derive admissible lookup heuristics from exact solutions of abstracted subproblems.
Automatically selecting abstractions is established prior work, so NEXTAI does not claim novelty for pattern databases or learned pattern choice alone.
relevance: The v5 experiment asks a narrower systems question: whether an observation-selected, mechanically certified two-constraint abstraction reduces exact induction work after construction, checking, memory and repeated-use costs are charged.
title: Automatic Generation of Memory Based Search Heuristics

claims_supported: Neural processes amortize Gaussian-process inference by replacing an exact cubic posterior calculation with a learned context-set map.
Finite representation, label contamination and amortization error remain separately identifiable costs rather than free inference savings.
relevance: Confirms that context-set amortization is established and that the existing NEXTAI set-memory and cross-family controls already test its bounded local analogue; it is not a new G1 mechanism by renaming pooling.
title: Three Costs of Amortizing Gaussian Process Inference with Neural Processes

claims_supported: Discrete Neural Algorithmic Reasoning separates predefined discrete algorithm states from continuous data flow.
Its correctness and OOD guarantees depend on explicit supervision of state transitions matching the classical algorithm.
relevance: The explicit state inventory and transition supervision are a supplied algorithm ontology, so this result cannot justify a family-blind NEXTAI quick on current whole-I/O cohorts.
title: Discrete Neural Algorithmic Reasoning

claims_supported: Learning to Condition trains a neural heuristic from solver traces to choose variable assignments for MPE inference.
The learned heuristic is integrated with exact conditioning or branch-and-bound search.
relevance: Maps directly to the already tested learned exact-search-guidance intervention; solver-trace supervision and branch ordering do not define a new NEXTAI causal family.
title: Learning to Condition: A Neural Heuristic for Scalable MPE Inference

claims_supported: Adaptive Mesh-Quantization allocates bit width spatially using a learned estimate of difficult PDE regions.
The paper reports quality-cost Pareto improvements over uniformly quantized neural PDE solvers across several PDE tasks.
relevance: Identifies a genuinely different hardware-aware computation-allocation factor, but NEXTAI lacks an immutable local PDE corpus, matched numerical solvers, bit-operation accounting and fixed-precision controls; it motivates a possible strategic reset rather than evidence or an immediate quick.
title: Adaptive Mesh-Quantization for Neural PDE Solvers

claims_supported: UGrid integrates learned multigrid components with residual-based self-supervision for linear PDE systems.
The method targets unseen problem sizes, boundary conditions and right-hand sides while retaining an iterative numerical-solver boundary.
relevance: Supports learned numerical solver structure as a potential distinct program, while also making classical multigrid, residual stopping, convergence and full solver cost mandatory controls absent from current NEXTAI cohorts.
title: UGrid: An Efficient-And-Rigorous Neural Multigrid Solver for Linear PDEs

claims_supported: Expire-Span learns when individual memories should expire rather than retaining every prior state.
The paper explicitly targets lower memory and attention cost on long sequences.
relevance: Direct prior art against treating learned destructive retention or memory expiry as an unoccupied computational principle.
title: Not All Memories are Created Equal: Learning to Forget by Expiring

claims_supported: PENCIL alternates generation with learned reduction that erases intermediate thoughts.
The claimed mechanism targets deeper computation with shorter active context.
relevance: Shows that generate-erase computation and experience-trained cleanup are existing causal ideas, not a novelty-first NEXTAI core.
title: PENCIL: Long Thoughts with Short Memory

claims_supported: Causal states are defined as the coarsest predictive partition of action-observation histories.
The learned continuous representation is connected theoretically to bisimulation.
relevance: Direct prior art for query- or behavior-induced quotient state, matching NEXTAI predictive-state and empirical-bisimulation mechanisms.
title: Learning Causal State Representations of Partially Observable Environments

claims_supported: Several state and history abstraction frameworks share the same self-predictive abstraction principle.
The paper derives a minimalist self-predictive representation learner for MDPs and POMDPs.
relevance: Strengthens causal deduplication of behavioral quotient representations across labels such as state abstraction, history abstraction and predictive state.
title: Bridging State and History Representations: Understanding Self-Predictive RL

claims_supported: Cellular sheaves assign local vector spaces and edge transport maps instead of assuming one trivial global graph geometry.
The restriction maps can be learned from data as part of a neural diffusion model.
relevance: Direct prior art for components with local coordinate systems connected by learned translations, excluding that causal core from novelty-first selection.
title: Neural Sheaf Diffusion: A Topological Perspective on Heterophily and Oversmoothing in GNNs

claims_supported: A conservative learned environment bound is refined using counterexamples returned by verification.
The approach can learn useful constraints without a complete environment model.
relevance: Direct prior art for competence acquired through counterexample-driven exclusion and verification rather than ordinary positive fitting.
title: Counter-example Guided Learning of Bounds on Environment Behavior

claims_supported: Equivalence-query learning identifies concepts by eliminating hypotheses using counterexamples.
Random counterexamples can reduce expected proper-query complexity in finite concept spaces.
relevance: Establishes counterexample-only version-space reduction as a mature learning-theoretic mechanism rather than a new NEXTAI core.
title: The Power of Random Counterexamples

claims_supported: Autotelic agents generate and pursue goals from intrinsic motivation rather than receiving a predefined external goal.
The paper studies decentralized goal alignment and emergent communication in a multi-agent setting.
relevance: Direct prior art for endogenous goal generation, showing that removing the externally supplied task is an established research program.
title: Autotelic Reinforcement Learning in Multi-Agent Environments

claims_supported: Proto-object structure is inferred from invariant regularities in anonymous sensorimotor experience without object labels.
The model builds a predictive sensorimotor graph and extracts densely connected structures.
relevance: Direct prior art for constructing object/interface semantics from interaction rather than receiving a fixed object ontology.
title: Identification of Invariant Sensorimotor Structures as a Prerequisite for the Discovery of Objects

claims_supported: Bidirectional Hebbian-style neuron and synapse update rules can be meta-learned without an explicit gradient input.
The learned local rules generalize to unseen training tasks in the reported experiments.
relevance: Direct prior art against claiming learned local non-backpropagation update laws as an unoccupied fundamental mechanism.
title: Meta-Learning Bidirectional Update Rules

claims_supported: A common independent latent source that is non-identifiable from either nonlinear view alone is identifiable from sufficiently distinct paired noisy views.
The recovery guarantee depends on paired correspondence, component-wise corruption, invertible mixing and a sufficiently-distinct-views variability condition.
relevance: Strong U1 contradiction showing exactly which candidate-visible relational signal can remove nonlinear observational ambiguity without factor labels.
title: The Incomplete Rosetta Stone problem: Identifiability results for Multi-view Nonlinear ICA

claims_supported: Under injective differentiable nonlinear mixing, a latent linear-Gaussian causal model is identifiable up to the stated ambiguities from non-paired single-node intervention regimes with unknown targets.
The guarantee requires intervention coverage of every latent node and knowledge of the observational dataset; acquisition cost is not part of the comparison.
relevance: Strong U1 contradiction that isolates exhaustive intervention-regime variation rather than target labels as the symmetry breaker.
title: Learning Linear Causal Representations from Interventions under General Nonlinear Mixing

claims_supported: Pairs of observations sharing an unknown subset of latent factors provide sufficient weak supervision for disentanglement under explicit assumptions.
The practical method does not require factor or group labels, and the learned representations were evaluated under controlled covariate shift and on other downstream tasks.
relevance: Joint U1/U2 contradiction whose causal ingredient is pairwise correspondence with sparse mechanism changes rather than a named architecture.
title: Weakly-Supervised Disentanglement Without Compromises

claims_supported: An invariant conditional predictor can be adversarially optimal for domain generalization when its conditional remains invariant in the unseen task.
Informative labeled environments can be used to select invariant subsets, but invariance in the unseen task is not testable from training data alone.
relevance: U2 contradiction and boundary case identifying informative environment variation and stable target conditionals as the required selection signal.
title: Invariant Models for Causal Transfer Learning

claims_supported: Equalizing risk across known training domains can improve robustness to more extreme shifts along represented directions.
REx has conditional successes on controlled shifts and reinforcement-learning tasks but is comparable to ERM and IRM on the reported standard DomainBed subset.
relevance: U2 contradiction with a clear condition: training-domain variation must span the direction of the later OOD shift.
title: Out-of-Distribution Generalization via Risk Extrapolation (REx)

claims_supported: The practical linear IRMv1 objective can miss natural invariances and generalize worse than ERM even on simple population problems.
Even a representation capturing the intended invariance can yield a suboptimal predictor when the loss is not invariant across environments.
relevance: Boundary evidence preventing conditional invariant-learning successes from being overstated as a general solution to NEXTAI U2.
title: Does Invariant Risk Minimization Capture Invariance?

title: The PGM-index: a fully-dynamic compressed learned index with provable worst-case bounds

title: Two-Level Adaptive Algebraic Multigrid for a Sequence of Problems with Slowly Varying Random Coefficients
